investigator.method: Level 1 PASSIVE_STATIC only: curl (plain HTTP GET, descriptive User-Agent, no authentication, no browser/JS execution) against the venue's own official '/programmation/' listing page and one linked event detail page. Both are plain server-rendered WordPress HTML with no schema.org Event JSON-LD (only generic Yoast SEO WebPage/Organization/BreadcrumbList JSON-LD) — every event's title/date/URL is directly present as static HTML text on both the listing page and its own detail page.

probe_history.reason: A plain curl GET of https://www.letrabendo.net/programmation/ immediately exposed static event cards, each with class="link-act event..." containing a full h2.date-event ('05 ― septembre 2026'), h3.name-event (title), and its own canonical event URL — no JS execution or further escalation needed. Note (found during offline-proof test-writing, retained honestly): the page renders every one of 67 distinct real events TWICE — once in the main chronological grid (plain class="link-act event") and again, byte-identically, inside a server-rendered 'Votre sélection' filter-section duplicate (class="link-act event bl-filt <month> <year> <type>" with an extra data-month attribute, used for client-side JS filtering) — 134 total card anchors, 67 distinct events after de-duplication by event URL. A second plain GET of one linked detail page (spectrum-waves) confirmed the same title/date directly and added a door-opening time ('Ouverture des portes 23:59') plus the sitewide footer address, all still via a plain static fetch. As due diligence this investigation also fetched /wp-json/ and /sitemap.xml (both plain unauthenticated GETs, still Level 1 in spirit) to check whether a cleaner structured feed existed for the site's 'programmation' custom post type; sitemap.xml confirms 'programmation' is a distinct post type (its own programmation-sitemap.xml) but no /wp/v2/programmation REST route is exposed, so no such feed exists — this did not change the SUFFICIENT verdict already reached from the static HTML cards themselves, only confirmed there is no better path to prefer.

venue_reference: Le Trabendo (concert/club venue, Parc de la Villette, 19th arrondissement, Paris)

identity.notes: Retained page's own <title> reads 'Programmation – Trabendo' at the venue's own domain letrabendo.net. The sitewide footer (present unchanged on both sampled pages) states 'Parc de la Villette / 211 avenue Jean Jaurès / 75019 Paris', matching the venue's known address, and every script/asset URL is self-hosted under www.letrabendo.net/wp-content/ — a self-consistent, first-party retained artifact.

site_classification.platform: WordPress (Yoast SEO plugin present — wp-json REST root is exposed but carries no queryable route for the site's own 'programmation' custom post type, confirmed via /wp-json/ and /sitemap.xml; a single generic Yoast WebPage/Organization/BreadcrumbList JSON-LD block is present but contains no schema.org Event data at all). The venue's own custom theme renders every event as a plain static HTML card (class="link-act event") on one listing page, with a matching detail page per event.

title.notes: The h3.name-event text on the listing card, confirmed identical on the event's own detail page heading.

start_date.notes: The h2.date-event text ('05 ― septembre 2026') is stated directly and identically on both the listing card and the event's own detail page — no context combination needed.

time.notes: Only a door-opening time is stated on the detail page ('Ouverture des portes 23:59'); no separate performance start time is given anywhere sampled. Treating this door time as a proven performance start would misattribute it (the same doorTime/startDate distinction already established for tempodrom-berlin-01), so this stays honestly PARTIAL rather than PROVEN.

end.notes: No end time or end date is stated anywhere on either sampled page.

venue_location.value: Le Trabendo, 211 Avenue Jean Jaurès, 75019 Paris (Parc de la Villette)
venue_location.notes: Neither sampled page repeats a full venue name+address directly beside the event card itself, but this is mechanically determinable: the site is a dedicated single-venue domain (letrabendo.net) with no other venue ever named anywhere sampled, and its own sitewide footer block — present unchanged on both the listing and detail page — states the venue's address directly.

derivation.rule: every event card and detail page on this dedicated single-venue domain belongs to the one venue named in that domain's own sitewide footer; concatenate the site's own footer address with that implied venue identity to get each event's venue_location
inputs: site is a single-venue dedicated domain (letrabendo.net) with no other venue referenced anywhere sampled
sitewide footer states 'Parc de la Villette / 211 avenue Jean Jaurès / 75019 Paris' identically on the listing and detail page

source_record_id.notes: No numeric ID is exposed on the card or detail page; the event's own WordPress permalink slug ('/programmation/spectrum-waves/') is this source's own canonical, self-referential path — the same documented judgement already established for tempodrom-berlin-01 and moog-barcelona-01/LAV (a permalink slug the source uses as its own canonical path).

event_url.notes: The card's own href, confirmed to resolve to the detail page sampled.

price.notes: No price is stated on either sampled page. Ticketing is delegated entirely to a third-party platform (shotgun.live) via an outbound 'Billetterie' link — a brief, bounded check of shotgun.live's own venue/event pages (https://shotgun.live/fr/venues/letrabendo and https://shotgun.live/events/spectrum-waves) returned HTTP 429 (rate-limited/blocked) on a single plain GET; per policy this was not retried or escalated (no brute-force probing of a third-party site), and third-party ticketing platforms are not treated as first-party authority for price in any case.

reasons: Identity PROVEN from a self-consistent retained artifact (page title, sitewide footer address, self-hosted assets, all at the venue's own domain).

title and start_date both PROVEN with basis DIRECT_SOURCE, stated directly and identically across both sampled pages.
